headline: Hot CPI and Waller's 50bp talk lift 2-year 17bp to 4.73%; gold -2%, WTI slips to $86.04
summary: A second straight 0.3% core CPI beat and Fed Governor Waller's call to consider a half-point December hike set off the biggest jump in the 2-year yield since April 2025, with the 10-year back at 5% after a soft auction. Gold fell about 2% and silver near 3% as the dollar and real yields rose. Oil eased to a two-month low on Iran de-escalation, while Bunds and OATs gave up a morning rally to follow Treasuries higher in yield.
drivers: Hot CPI and a hawkish Waller reprice the Fed

October CPI rose 0.4% (0.3% expected) and core 0.3% (0.2% expected), a third month at that pace. Waller said a 50bp December hike should be considered if core ran at 0.3% or more, Logan wants at least two more hikes, and swaps moved to fully price a December hike with a small chance of 50bp; the 2-year rose about 17bp to 4.73%.
Soft 10-year auction puts 5% back on the board

The $42bn 10-year sale cleared at 5.02%, above pre-auction trading, with dealers left 9.7%, the most since May. The 10-year rose about 12bp to near 5.00% and the 30-year 9bp to 5.35%, so the curve bear-flattened with 2s10s near 26bp.
Iran de-escalation keeps oil near two-month lows

Trump said more military action against Iran is not needed for now. WTI fell 81¢ to $86.04 and Brent $1.08 to $91.49 after being down over $3, as Iran's Rezaei said no talks are under way; RBOB fell to its lowest since March and the AAA pump average dropped below $4.
Stronger dollar and real yields hit metals

Comex gold settled $84 lower at $4,020.70 and spot ended near $4,030, while silver lost 2.8% to $51.10. Euro-area yields reversed a morning rally as the US move spilled over and ECB's Lane backed a December hike; the Bund 10-year rose 3bp to 3.30% and the French 10-year 4bp to 4.78%.

oil.note: Dec WTI settled -81¢ (-0.9%) at $86.04, lowest since Aug 31, after trading near $85; Brent -$1.08 at $91.49.
oil.why: Trump said further US military action against Iran is not needed for now, extending Monday's 4.4% slide, and WTI was down more than $3 early. Prices pared losses after Iran's Mohsen Rezaei said no negotiations with Washington are under way, and Gulf shipping attacks continue. The EIA's STEO still sees Brent near $100 for the rest of the year with US crude stocks at 410m barrels, the lowest end-October level since 2014.
oil.outlook: Bias lower in an $82–90 range while the Iran pause holds and Hormuz flows keep improving; $85 is near support and a break opens the low $80s. Eurasia Group sees Brent holding near $90 without a deal, and a serious tanker attack would push WTI back above $90.
oil.watch: Iran headlines, OPEC report Wed Nov 11, EIA stocks Thu Nov 12 and the IEA report Fri Nov 13.

gas.note: Dec RBOB fell 4.21¢ (-1.6%) to $2.6088, the lowest settle since Mar 4; ULSD -2.0% to $4.1309.
gas.why: Gasoline followed crude lower on the Iran pause and is now down about 6% in two sessions and 21% this month. Winter-grade blends and weak post-season demand give it little support. The AAA national average fell to about $3.98, below $4 for the first time since July and 17¢ lower than a week ago, while CPI showed the gasoline index up only 1% in October after a 9.1% jump in September.
gas.outlook: Bias lower in a $2.50–2.72 range while WTI stays under $90; pump prices should drift toward $3.85–3.90 by Thanksgiving. A crude rebound above $90 would lift RBOB back toward $2.75–2.80.
gas.watch: EIA gasoline stocks and refinery runs Thu Nov 12, AAA pump average and Iran headlines.

gold.note: Comex Nov settled -$84.30 (-2.1%) at $4,020.70, lowest since Nov 3; spot near $4,030 after a $4,149 Asian high.
gold.why: The hot CPI and Waller's half-point hike talk lifted the dollar and real yields, which raises the cost of holding non-yielding bullion; the 10-year real yield is near 2.6%. Markets moved to fully price a December hike and added bets on at least two hikes by mid-2027. Weak positioning made the fall sharper: Comex speculators cut net longs for an eighth week and gold ETFs have seen outflows for four weeks.
gold.outlook: Bias lower in a $3,950–4,120 range while hike pricing builds; $4,000 is key support and a close below it opens $3,900. A soft PPI or a quick dollar pullback would take it back toward $4,100.
gold.watch: US PPI Fri Nov 13, Fed speakers, the dollar and real yields.

silver.note: Comex Nov settled -$1.46 (-2.8%) at $51.10, the lowest since Nov 3; spot near $51.3–51.5.
silver.why: Silver fell more than gold on the same mix of a firmer dollar, higher real yields and repricing toward faster Fed hikes. It gave back Monday's rally because early tech-stock weakness hit its industrial side, though a late chip rebound limited the damage. The gold/silver ratio moved back toward 79.
silver.outlook: Range of about $49.50–53 with a mild downward bias while yields rise; a break of $50 would retest the October low near $49. A rebound above $53 needs a softer dollar or strong tech demand.
silver.watch: US PPI Nov 13, chip stocks, the dollar and China trade data.

us2y.note: Up about 17bp to near 4.73%, the biggest one-day jump since April 2025.
us2y.why: October core CPI rose 0.3% against 0.2% expected for a third straight month, about 3.7% annualised. Waller said that pace argues for considering a 50bp hike in December and that only 25bp would risk the Fed's credibility, and Logan called for at least two more 25bp hikes. Swaps went from about 85% to fully pricing a December hike, with a small chance of 50bp.
us2y.outlook: Bias higher in a 4.65–4.85% range while officials push for hikes; a firm PPI and more 50bp talk would target 4.85%. A soft PPI or Fed leaders pushing back on a larger move would pull it back toward 4.65%.
us2y.watch: PPI Fri Nov 13, Fed speakers and the Dec 8–9 FOMC.

us5y.note: Up about 15bp to near 4.83% as hike bets for 2027 were rebuilt.
us5y.why: The belly sold off almost as much as the 2-year because markets added hikes beyond December, with at least two moves now priced by mid-2027. Waller said higher rates are needed sooner rather than later, at minimum to undo last year's three insurance cuts. Lower oil did little to help as core inflation, not energy, drove the surprise.
us5y.outlook: Bias higher in a 4.75–4.92% range; a hot PPI or more hawkish Fed speakers would test 4.92%, while a dovish pushback from leadership would bring 4.75%.
us5y.watch: PPI Nov 13 and Fed speakers before the December blackout.

us10y.note: Up about 12bp to near 5.00%; the $42bn 10-year auction cleared at 5.02%.
us10y.why: The CPI beat pushed the 10-year about 11bp higher before the auction, and the sale then tailed, clearing at 5.02% with a 2.46 bid-to-cover, foreign-type buyers down to 61% from 77% in August, and dealers left with 9.7%. The curve bear-flattened to about 26bp in 2s10s because hikes are expected to contain long-run inflation.
us10y.outlook: Range of 4.90–5.10% with an upward bias while hike pricing builds; above 5.10% opens October's highs near 5.3%. ING sees value near 5%, and a soft PPI would bring 4.90%.
us10y.watch: Bond market closed Wed Nov 11, 30-year auction Thu Nov 12 and PPI Fri Nov 13.

us30y.note: Up about 9bp to 5.35%, the highest close since Oct 28 and the smallest rise on the curve.
us30y.why: The long bond rose less than the front end because markets see a more aggressive Fed as protection against lasting inflation, which flattens the curve. The soft 10-year auction still weighed, as it hints at weak demand for Thursday's $25bn 30-year sale. Lower oil helped limit the damage.
us30y.outlook: Range of 5.28–5.45% with a flattening bias; a weak 30-year auction would test 5.45%, while a solid one and a soft PPI would bring 5.28%.
us30y.watch: 30-year auction Thu Nov 12 and PPI Fri Nov 13.

de2y.note: Up about 6bp to near 3.07%, the biggest daily rise in over a month, after a morning dip.
de2y.why: Schatz yields fell early on lower oil, then jumped after the hot US CPI spilled over into euro rates. ECB chief economist Lane said a December hike would be prudent if the outlook holds and that inflation has not yet peaked, lifting market odds of a December hike to about 75% from 66% on Monday, with a hike fully priced by February.
de2y.outlook: Bias higher in a 3.00–3.15% range while ECB hike pricing builds; a hot German or euro-area inflation print would test 3.15%. Brent staying below $90 is the main reason it could ease back to 3.00%.
de2y.watch: German final CPI Wed Nov 11, euro-area GDP Fri Nov 13, ECB speakers and the ECB Dec 17.

de5y.note: Up about 5bp to near 3.12% as the morning rally reversed.
de5y.why: The 5-year traded lower early on cheaper energy, then sold off with Treasuries after the CPI beat and Lane's backing for a December hike. Higher odds of ECB tightening into early 2027 moved the belly almost as much as the front end.
de5y.outlook: Range of 3.05–3.20% with a slight upward bias; a hot euro-area print or more hawkish ECB talk would test 3.20%, while lower oil keeps 3.05% in reach.
de5y.watch: German CPI Nov 11, euro-area GDP Nov 13 and ECB speakers.

de10y.note: Up about 3bp to near 3.30% after dipping to about 3.24% in the morning.
de10y.why: Bunds rallied early as oil fell, then reversed after the hot US CPI sent Treasury yields 12bp higher; the Bund future fell about 0.5%. The 10-year rose much less than the 2-year because lower energy prices still cap long-run inflation expectations in Europe, so the curve flattened.
de10y.outlook: Range of 3.22–3.36% with a slight upward bias while US yields climb; a break above 3.36% would need a 10-year Treasury above 5.10% or hawkish ECB news.
de10y.watch: German CPI Nov 11, euro-area GDP and Fitch's Germany review Nov 13.

de30y.note: Up about 2bp to near 3.65%, the smallest move on the German curve.
de30y.why: The long end rose less than shorter bonds because a more hawkish ECB and lower oil both support long-run inflation control. Heavy German issuance to fund fiscal expansion still keeps a premium in 30-year debt, and the 9bp rise in the US 30-year limited any rally.
de30y.outlook: Range of 3.60–3.72% with a flattening bias near term; a break above 3.72% would need a long-end selloff in Treasuries or an oil spike.
de30y.watch: US 30-year auction Nov 12, German supply and ECB speakers.

fr2y.note: Up about 5bp to near 3.53%, tracking the jump in Schatz yields.
fr2y.why: Short OATs follow ECB pricing, so they rose with German 2-year yields once US CPI and Lane's comments lifted December hike odds to about 75%. French fiscal risk plays little role at this maturity, so the move mirrored Germany's.
fr2y.outlook: Range of 3.45–3.60% with a slight upward bias while ECB hike pricing firms; a lasting oil drop that cools inflation is the main downside trigger.
fr2y.watch: French final CPI Fri Nov 13, ECB speakers and the ECB Dec 17.

fr5y.note: Up about 5bp to near 4.18% after a morning rally on lower energy.
fr5y.why: The 5-year OAT gained early as cheaper energy eased France's growth and deficit worries, then followed Bunds and Treasuries lower in price after the US CPI beat. Its spread to Germany held steady, as Moody's decision last week to keep France's rating still supports demand.
fr5y.outlook: Range of 4.10–4.25% with a flat spread to Bunds; a setback in the Senate budget debate would push it toward 4.25%.
fr5y.watch: Senate budget debate, French CPI Nov 13 and rating reviews.

fr10y.note: Up about 4bp to near 4.78% after a morning low of 4.71%; spread to Bunds near 148bp.
fr10y.why: OATs led the morning rally, with the 10-year falling to its lowest since late September and the Bund spread narrowing to about 142bp, the tightest in three weeks, as cheaper energy eased deficit fears. The US CPI beat and Lane's hike signal then reversed the gains, and the spread widened a little as investors cut exposure to riskier euro bonds.
fr10y.outlook: Range of 4.68–4.85% with the spread held near 140–155bp; a budget passed even by decree could tighten it toward 140bp, while a government crisis would push it above 160bp.
fr10y.watch: Senate budget debate, the Dec 9 Senate vote and rating reviews.

fr30y.note: Up about 5bp to near 5.32%, giving back last week's gains.
fr30y.why: The 30-year OAT followed global long-end yields higher after the US CPI beat, and it rose more than the German 30-year because long French debt carries the most fiscal risk, with deficits near 5% of GDP. The weak US 10-year auction also hurt demand for long bonds before Thursday's US 30-year sale.
fr30y.outlook: Range of 5.22–5.40% with a bias to lag shorter OATs; a credible budget deal could pull it to 5.22%, while political trouble risks a retest of the highs.
fr30y.watch: Senate budget debate, OAT auctions and the US 30-year auction Nov 12.

watch: Next: US bond market closed, OPEC report and German final CPI Wed Nov 11, US 30-year auction and EIA stocks Thu Nov 12, US PPI, euro-area GDP, French CPI and the IEA report Fri Nov 13, then the Fed Dec 8–9 and ECB Dec 17.
